3.1.8 Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE)

Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE) was established at a cost of Rs.12.65 crore (Rs.10.00 crore under TANII fund and remaining Rs.2.65 crore from Service/Commitment Charges). The Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE) was inaugurated on 28.02.2026.

TNPAGE aims to transform governance into an interactive and dynamic process, enabling Government departments to test interventions, explore scenario-based policy modelling and drive

81

data-driven decision-making with unprecedented precision.

TNPAGE is first of its kind Governance Knowledge and Experiential Centre, designed as a public knowledge space that presents Government policies, development indicators and governance outcomes in an immersive and accessible format.

The Centre also includes the Tamil Nadu Policy Portal - the Strategy Room at TNPAGE will serve as a dedicated space for policy discussions, planning and collaborative decision making, supported by advanced data visualisations and analytical tools. Through interactive dashboards, maps and thematic visualisations, it enables policymakers and researchers to explore key socio-economic indicators, track development trends and gain insights that support informed and evidence-based policy formulation for Tamil Nadu.

extracts.title: G.O.(Ms) No.157: Urban Development - Mandating the preparation, approval and adoption of legally valid GIS-based Master Plans, Zonal Plans and Land Use Plans - Establishment of a regulatory framework for standardized methodologies and GIS data layers - Orders - Issued.
extracts.text:
a. Adoption of legally valid GIS-based Master, zonal, and land use plans.

To institutionalize and standardize these initiatives across all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Planning Authorities (UDA) it is proposed to mandate the preparation, approval, and adoption of GIS-based Master Plans, including Zonal Plans and Land Use Plans. All concerned authorities shall be required to follow standardized spatial and attribute structures, obtain statutory approval from the competent authority, and ensure formal adoption under relevant planning laws.

b. All ULBs/Authorities are directed to upload approved GIS based Plans for public access.

Further, all ULBs and UDAs shall be mandated to upload approved GIS-based plans on their official web portals and ensure public accessibility through user-friendly platforms.

c. Regulatory framework shall be established.

It is also proposed to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework defining the methodology, spatial standards and regulations of master plan preparation encompassing the processes such as baseline study with benchmarks, preparation of base map, preparation of existing land use map, existing situation analysis, identification of gaps and demands, stakeholders engagement, development proposals, preparation of proposed land use map, formulating the draft master plan and notifying final master plan using a standard operating procedure to ensure compliance and accountability.

Spatial Standards are as follows:

e Mapping Scale ~ Master Plan: 1:4,000; Zonal Plan: 1:2,000; Local Area Plan (LAP): 1:1,000; Site Plan: 1:500

e Horizontal Datum: World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84)

e Map Projection: Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM)

e Vertical Datum: WGS 84 Ellipsoidal Height, converted to Mean Sea Level (MSL) using an appropriate Geoid Model.

d. The spatial database shall include comprehensive GIS layers such as administrative boundaries, cadastral parcels (where available), transportation networks, existing and proposed land use, building footprints, water bodies, drainage, contours and terrain, utilities (water supply, sewerage, storm water, electricity, gas, telecommunications), environmental features, heritage assets, public and community facilities, green and open spaces, disasterprone areas, infrastructure corridors, and demographic and socioeconomic attributes linked through spatial identifiers.

e. The implementation of the above measures will result in a standardized, transparent, and legally robust planning system, enabling efficient urban development and improved governance. It will also strengthen public access to planning information and support data-driven decision-making.

4. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government to issue necessary orders for mandating the preparation, approval, and adoption of legally valid GISbased Master Plans, Zonal Plans, and Land Use Plans, and directing all ULBs/Authorities to upload the approved GIS-based plans for public access, and for the establishment of a regulatory framework for standardized methodologies and GIS data layers.

8.2 Disease Prevention Services

Vaccination is one of the most effective ways

of protecting livestock from infectious diseases.

Regular immunisation against major diseases

such as Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD),

Brucellosis, Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD), Anthrax,

Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS), Black Quarter

(BQ), Sheep Pox and Peste des Petits Ruminants

(PPR) helps prevent disease outbreaks, reduces

47

economic losses to farmers and improves the

health and productivity of livestock.

These vaccination programmes are

implemented under various Central Sector

Schemes like National Animal Diseases Control

Programme and Assistance to States for Control

of Animal Diseases form an important part of the

State's animal health strategy.

8.2.1 National Animal Disease Control

Programme (NADCP)

NADCP is a Central Sector Scheme aimed at

eliminating Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) and

Brucellosis through systematic vaccination of

eligible cattle and buffaloes.

8.2.1.1 Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD)

Vaccination Programme

FMD is a highly contagious viral disease that

affects cloven-hoofed animals, leading to reduced

48

milk production, poor growth and significant

economic losses. The disease is controlled

through bi-annual vaccination, supported by

biosecurity measures and regulated movement of

animals.

Since 2020, nine rounds of FMD vaccination

have been completed up to August 2026, covering

83.49 lakh eligible bovines across Tamil Nadu.

8.2.1.2 Brucellosis Vaccination Programme

Brucellosis is a bacterial disease that causes

abortions, stillbirths and infertility in cattle,

resulting in considerable economic losses to

farmers. To protect future breeding stock, female

calves aged 4 to 8 months are vaccinated once in

their lifetime. Five phases of the Brucellosis

Vaccination Programme have been completed till

2024-25, covering 24 lakh heifer calves across

the State.

49

8.2.2 Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD)

LSD is a viral disease that affects cattle and

buffaloes. It causes fever, skin nodules and a

sharp decline in milk production, adversely

affecting farmers' incomes.

To protect the State's cattle population,

59.11 lakh cattle were vaccinated against Lumpy

Skin Disease during 2025–26 using Goat Pox

vaccine (GPV), significantly reducing the risk of

disease outbreaks.

19. Focus Areas and New Schemes

The Department is committed to

transforming livestock rearing from a subsistence

activity into a sustainable and remunerative

enterprise. In the coming years, the Department

will concentrate on the following focus areas:

 Enhancing livestock productivity through

targeted breeding, nutrition and animal

health interventions.

 Achieving green fodder self-sufficiency to

ensure year-round feed security.

 Conserving and improving indigenous

livestock breeds with emphasis on genetic

improvement.

104

 Expanding livestock insurance coverage to

reduce production risks and provide greater

income security to farmers.

 Modernising veterinary infrastructure and

strengthening disease diagnosis and

surveillance.

 Promoting livestock-based entrepreneurship

through meat processing, value addition

and improved market access.

 Advancing animal welfare, strengthening

rabies control, safeguarding public health

and promoting responsible pet ownership.

These focus areas will guide the

Department's efforts towards building a

productive, climate-resilient and farmer-centric

livestock sector that contributes meaningfully to

rural prosperity and the State's agricultural

growth.

105

Livestock Productivity

will remain the Department's foremost priority.

Latest breeding interventions will be intensified to

enhance the genetic potential of livestock,

particularly in backward districts, through free

breeding services, expanded use of sex-sorted

semen and introduction of superior breeding bulls

under the Frozen Semen Programme.

Livelihood opportunities will be strengthened

by supporting eligible beneficiaries with milch

cows, sheep and goats. Special emphasis will be

placed on promoting buffalo rearing to augment

milk production, while region-specific

interventions will encourage piggery, rabbit

rearing and other small livestock enterprises as

viable supplementary sources of income, thereby

strengthening the rural economy.

for women living in rural areas, milch cows

will be provided at no cost to 10,000

crore. These initiatives will enhance the

livelihoods of rural marginalised women.

 Further, 100 small-scale native chicken

poultry units will be established with 50%

107

crore.

ensuring nutritional security across the State.

entrepreneurship among small and marginal milk

producers and ensuring a sustainable source of income,

500 medium-scale dairy farms, each comprising five milch

animals (3+2 model), will be established. Under this

scheme, a capital subsidy of 25 per cent of the project

interest rates will be facilitated for the remaining project

cost. This initiative will enhance milk production, generate

year-round employment and improve the livelihoods of

be provided from the state fund for the implementation of

this scheme.

ii. Mini Dairies

To ensure a stable year-round income for milk

provided for the establishment of 5,000 Mini Dairy units

milk producers under the Mini Dairy Scheme, the

programme will be continued during 2026–27 with a

financial allocation of Rs.4.19 crore.

With the objective of reducing the cost of milk

production and supporting economically weaker milk

producers, quality balanced cattle feed will be supplied to

eligible milk producers living below the poverty line at a

subsidy of Rs.2/- per kilogram, at the rate of 3 kg per

animal per day for 300 days. This scheme will promote

scientific feed management practices, enhance milk

productivity, and improve the income of milk producers.

implementation of this scheme.

Healthy heifer calves are the foundation of future milk

reproductive performance, and lifetime productivity of

year at 50 per cent subsidy to 50,000 heifer calves.
